Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: The grandparent notices their grandchild seems to be feeling lost or discouraged about a personal matter.
Expectation2: Secure packages and confirm successful delivery
Situation2: Hand-delivering a high-value or sensitive package directly to the recipient and verifying their identity
Story: I was halfway through my delivery route when my phone buzzed with a message from my daughter: “Can you check on Jamie? He’s been quiet all morning.” I glanced at the next address—an urgent, high-value package that required a signature and ID check. As I pulled up to the recipient’s house, my mind wandered to Jamie, my grandson. He’d seemed withdrawn lately, and I knew from experience that sometimes a gentle word or a listening ear could make all the difference. But the package in my hands was marked “sensitive—deliver in person.” My supervisor had stressed the importance of these deliveries, especially after last week’s mix-up. I could feel the weight of both roles pressing on me: the expectation to be the reliable, wise grandparent Jamie needed, and the dependable delivery person my job demanded. My heart ached to call Jamie, to offer comfort and guidance, but the package in my hands reminded me of the trust placed in me by my employer. I stood at the doorstep, torn between the needs of my family and the responsibilities of my work, uncertain which to answer first.
